stage: the LoRA scene-lever bake-off — two arms, one seed, the E12 wave-3 record as baseline
registered_by: executor seat, on E14-run, BEFORE the first submission of any E14 graph and committed ahead of it
how_this_was_chosen: Not chosen — inherited. 2026081233 is E12 wave 3's seed 1, which is E11 wave 3's seed before that. The spec pins it so the bake-off's only generation-reaching difference from the E12 wave-3 record is the LoRA. A fresh number would make every arm a two-variable read against the baseline it is compared to.

allocation.2026081233: the ONLY seed, run once per arm. Arm T and arm S each execute this number against the byte-pinned E12 wave-3 graph plus their own LoRA insertions.

why_one_seed_does_not_violate_the_two_se: E10's closing ruling R3 binds: a scene observation from ONE seed is an observation, never a route property. This experiment is a bake-off and therefore claims NO property — its outputs are candidates for the Director's eye. Whichever look he picks earns the property-grade follow-on (the strength sweep, two seeds, its own spec). The law is respected by not making the claim, not by evading the count.
the_inert_second_seed: The low-noise expert's KSamplerAdvanced carries noise_seed 0 with add_noise=disable. It draws nothing, so it is inert; route_gates.gate_s_registration reports it and does not demand it be registered. Recorded here so a reader of the graph does not find an unregistered 0 and take it for a gap in this list. Carried verbatim from specs/E12-seeds.json, where the same graph made the same note.
binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. armature_core/gates.py::gate_s_seed_registration enforces both clauses at build time and armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces them again against the saved file the cloud actually executes.

ceiling.note: TWO generations, one per arm. No re-runs. A fired gate or a platform rejection ends THAT arm as a finding and the other proceeds; arms are independent. estimate_credits is recorded before each submission and any partner-credit estimate above 0 halts. On an all-OSS graph it returns 0 by construction, so the ceiling is enforced by counting generations. Spent GPU time has no compensator; the bound is the honest treatment.
ceiling.why_machine_readable: The value was free prose and no tool under tools/ read the key, while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated. CLAUDE.md makes the credit ceiling a per-spec obligation and records that spent credits have no compensator, so the one unrecoverable resource in this repo was bounded by a string nothing could parse. The prose is not deleted: it is `note`, verbatim, and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it. CORRECTION, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 8, F-6c5c537b). This paragraph used to argue the fix with the clause “while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated”, and to close “and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it”. Both halves were measured on the tree and only one survived. `grep -rn allocation tools/ --include=*.py` returns 0 hits: `allocation` has no reader at all, so it is exactly as unread as `ceiling` was when it was filed. `seeds` has seven readers — build_animate_payload.py:482 (main), build_camera_i2v_payload.py:1110 (main), build_i2v_payload.py:687 (main), build_lora_arm_payload.py:463 (gate_s), build_r2v_payload.py:272 (build_and_write), build_t2v_payload.py:496 (main) and gate_saved_graph.py:602 (main) — each handing the list to a seed gate, so that half of the claim holds. And no tool reads `ceiling` from a seeds spec either: every `ceiling` hit under tools/ is `armature_core.assembly`'s unrelated CASCADE slot ceiling, or a builder passing that one. So `ceiling.submissions` is a number a submission step COULD count against and none does today — the bound is held by the spec and the executor, not by code. The original claim is kept above rather than deleted, because the correction is more useful than the original. tests/test_seeds_specs.py pins the measurement; the day a builder counts against `ceiling.submissions`, that test flips with it and this paragraph is rewritten again. RE-ANCHORED, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 14). Three of the seven citations moved because gates were added above their readers, and the line numbers were RE-MEASURED rather than re-typed: build_i2v_payload.py 620 -> 687 (start_image_record gained the fit_disagrees_with_the_file andon, F-e17613c2), build_r2v_payload.py 217 -> 272 (Gate CEILING gained its behaviour-keyed hosted-node census, F-eec3f145), and gate_saved_graph.py 487 -> 602 (route_facts reads the two facts Gate ROUTE needs off the builder's payload record, F-2da88c51). The other four are unmoved. The function name beside each number is the anchor that survives the next move; tests/test_seeds_specs.py checks the pair, which is how this drift was found.
